scores.claim_text: In fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, 98% of SAIC's total revenues were attributable to prime contracts with the U.S. government or to subcontracts with other contractors engaged in work for the U.S. government.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts shows 1,280,019 SAIC DoD awards totaling $10.79B — confirms SAIC is a real, durable USG prime
scores.interpretation: Macro USG-revenue concentration is corroborated. Top awards include large multi-year Army RDECOM software-engineering, simulation, and CCE follow-on contracts — diversified across DoW components, not single-program-dependent.

scores.claim_text: Approximately 52% of SAIC's total revenues were attributable to the Department of War (formerly DoD).
supports: usaspending confirms massive DoD prime footprint
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND — corpus by_entity index has zero SAIC entries; SAIC is not a primary contractor on any of the 410 RDT&E/Procurement PEs seeded in the corpus
scores.interpretation: Coverage gap, not a red flag. SAIC's revenue is overwhelmingly services-and-IT-modernization (cost-reimbursable task orders against IDIQ vehicles like OASIS), which lives in O&M and unique PE families not in the 410-PE seeded corpus.

scores.claim_text: SAIC's Defense and Intelligence segment provides a diverse portfolio of national security solutions to DoW and the IC, including IT modernization, digital engineering, AI, mission systems support, training-and-simulation, and ground vehicles support.
supports: SAIC names CAPABILITY CATEGORIES, not Program Elements — by design, the J-Book divergence pattern cannot fire because there is no named PE to test
scores.interpretation: META-OBSERVATION: SAIC's 10-K narrative is deliberately category-level rather than program-level. This is the OPPOSITE of the IonQ/Wolfpack short-thesis pattern — those targets named specific PEs that proved to be zeroed. SAIC's diversified, services-heavy mix means no single PE can sink the forward narrative.

scores.claim_text: Ground Vehicles Support: SAIC integrates, modifies, upgrades and sustains ground vehicles for U.S. armed forces.
supports: Major ground-vehicle programs (Bradley, Stryker, Abrams) NOT_FOUND in the seeded 410-PE corpus — these live in Army Procurement P-40 lines not currently in the J-Book index
scores.interpretation: Coverage gap. SAIC's ground-vehicle work is broad sustainment, not concentrated on any single platform; even if PEs were covered, materiality would be diluted. Not load-bearing in the forward narrative.

scores.claim_text: Next Generation Space: SAIC integrates advanced solutions to enable rapid deployment of future space missions.
supports: pentagon_jbook hit on SDA Transport Layer family: T3 Transport Layer (PE 1206410SF) is UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS; SDA Transport T0-T2 is FUNDED_SHRINKING; SDA being dissolved with mission rolling into Starshield (SpaceX sole-source). Space Test Program (PE 1206864SF) FUNDED_STEADY.
scores.M_value: SDA Transport Layer → primary match UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS (T3), secondary FUNDED_SHRINKING (T0-T2); SDA Tracking Layer NOT_FOUND; Space Test Program FUNDED_STEADY ($28.8M FY26)
scores.interpretation: SDA programs are shrinking/being absorbed into a sole-sourced SpaceX backbone, and SDA itself is dissolving as a standalone agency. SAIC's 'Next Generation Space' offering is exposed to that pipeline at the integrator/services level. However: SAIC is NOT listed as a primary contractor on T3 Transport (primaries are York, LMT, NOC), and Space Test Program (where SAIC has historic exposure) is steady. Materiality is bounded — downgrade to MODERATE per heuristic 2 (subcontractor / pipeline narrative, not booked prime revenue).

scores.claim_text: Spending packages (infrastructure bill, IRA, CHIPS) may provide additional opportunity in digital modernization, cyber, microelectronics support, and climate resiliency.
supports: earmark_detector returned NOT_EARMARK for CHIPS microelectronics — these are not single-sponsor earmarks but broad authorization programs
scores.interpretation: Aspirational language ("may provide additional opportunity"). Non-binding. Cannot be verified or falsified via J-Book — these are authorization-act funds outside the RDT&E/Procurement J-Book lens.

scores.claim_text: SAIC acquired SilverEdge Government Solutions on October 15, 2025 for ~$203M cash, advancing strategy to provide mission-focused solutions and commercial products.
supports: usaspending shows ZERO DoD contracts under the literal name 'SilverEdge Government Solutions' — likely doing-business-as subsidiaries; acq_coherence call failed on schema mismatch (needs parent_thesis/acquisitions)
scores.interpretation: Zero direct USAspending hit suggests SilverEdge operates under subsidiary names not entity-resolved in this run. Not necessarily a red flag for a small bolt-on (~$203M), but the lack of orthogonal contract footprint means we cannot independently confirm the acquired revenue base. Coherence test could not complete.

scores.claim_text: SAIC serves customers through approximately 1,700 active contracts and task orders and employs approximately 23,000 individuals.
supports: 1.28M historical USAspending records over the full lookback and >$10B in obligations is fully consistent with a 1,700-active-contract, 23K-employee prime — fragmentation ratio is plausible
scores.interpretation: Operational-scale claim is corroborated. The very fragmentation that makes J-Book verification hard (no single PE concentration) is also what protects SAIC from the single-PE-zeroing failure mode.

scores.claim_text: SAIC occupies approximately 3 million square feet of leased floor space.
scores.M_check: n/a — no facility query run; out of scope for J-Book cohort
scores.interpretation: Control claim. Cannot be verified within the J-Book cohort scope; not load-bearing.

scores.claim_text: Effective January 31, 2026, SAIC consolidated five business groups into three — second reorganization since fiscal 2025.
supports: Two reorganizations in 24 months may be a soft governance signal but is not testable via pentagon_jbook
scores.interpretation: Note for narrative: repeated segment reshuffles can obscure year-over-year program-level comparability and can be a flag for organic-growth weakness, but no J-Book hook exists. Treat as context, not a J-Book divergence.

summary.framework_finding: DIVERGENCE_PATTERN_DOES_NOT_FIT — SAIC's 10-K is deliberately category-level (IT modernization, digital engineering, AI, training-sim, ground vehicles, next-gen space) and names ZERO Program Elements or PE numbers. The J-Book divergence pattern requires named programs to test against, and SAIC's services-heavy, IDIQ-task-order revenue model (1.28M awards, $10.79B cumulative DoD) is structurally diversified.
summary.best_signal: Indirect: SAIC's 'Next Generation Space' narrative touches an area where the J-Book corpus shows SDA Transport Layer T3 UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS and SDA dissolving into Starshield sole-source. SAIC is not a primary on T3, so exposure is bounded (MODERATE).
summary.coverage_gaps: J-Book by_entity has zero SAIC entries. The 410-PE corpus is concentrated on RDT&E + select Space Force/Air Force lines; SAIC's revenue lives in O&M, intel-community services, and Army software-engineering task orders that the corpus does not index.
